To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proton cage of L1 encapsulates perchlorate, hexafluorophosphate, hexafluoroarsenate, hexafluoronitrate, hexafluorsilicate and hydrogen sulfate in their anionic states.

the octaprotonation of octaaminophenyl-cryptand L1 results in encapsulation of inorganic anionic species such as perchlorates, hydrogen sulfates and hexafluoro silicates inside the cavity of the cage in a monotopic mode.
the encapsulation of tetra- and octa- anionic species by proton cage of octamethyl substituted octaaminocrytand is possible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural aspects of the proton cage of the macrocyclic receptor L1 and its interaction with the inorganic guests such as perchlorates, hexafluoroborates and hydrogen sulfate.
the structural studies on the encapsulation of anions inside a protonated cage of L 1 and the conformation of the host is dependent on the nature and size of the encapsulated anion.
the structural aspects of the binding modes of anions with proton cages of octaaminobenzene cryptands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the octaprotonation of L1 is the most stable and the most preferred protonation state for the encapsulation of inorganic anion.

the protonated octaammonium cage L1 encapsulates anions of tetrahedral (ClO4−) or octahedral (HSiF6) symmetry via hydrogen bonding with the cage protons, whereas the hydrogen sulfate anion (SO42−) is encapsulated by the cage protons and the hydrogen bonding with the host cage protons is not the sole factor for the encapsulation of SO42− by L1.

encapsulation of anions inside the cage of protonated octa-aminocryptand is possible and it can be achieved by the combination of different types of hydrogen bonds, namely N–H·· ·O, N–H··O··O, O–H··O and C–H·· ·X (X = F, O).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the octaaminocyclotetraphosphine cryptand L1, in protonated state, encapsulates the inorganic anions via multiple hydrogen bonds and the conformation of the cryptand in octaprotonation is spherical in nature.
the octaprotonation of L1 is the most favorable state for encapsulation of the anions.
the proton cage of L1 is able to encapsulate a variety of anions with the help of hydrogen bonding and other weak interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protonated cryptands can be used as efficient receptors for anion encapsulation and the encapsulated anions are stabilized inside the cage via a combination of hydrogen bonds.
protonated L1 is able to encapsulate a range of inorganic anion species, including tetrahedral and hexahedral anions, in its proton cage.

the encapsulation of inorganic anion inside the cavity of proton cage of octaminocryptand is a general feature of these complexes and the encapsulated anion does not show any specific interaction with the cage of L in the final conformation.
